summary: Narrator and family visit Ron Glover, Darryl's father, in a messy apartment to tell him Darryl is alive and held prisoner on Treasure Island. Ron reacts with shock and embarrassment, then agrees to come with them to the Bay Guardian reporter Barbara Stratford to tell Darryl's story. Ron changes into a military dress uniform, and the group drives down the 101 to Mountain View, reflecting on the contrast with the narrator's own Bay Area.
one_line: The narrator's family tells Ron Glover that his son Darryl is alive and imprisoned on Treasure Island, then drives to reporter Barbara Stratford.
key_facts: Darryl's father, Ron Glover, sat like a statue while the narrator explained the note's contents.
The narrator told Ron: "Darryl is alive and being held prisoner on Treasure Island."
Ron stuffed his fist in his mouth and made a horrible groaning sound upon hearing the news.
The narrator's father said the family has a friend who writes for the Bay Guardian, an investigative reporter.
The Bay Guardian is described as a free weekly that often lost its reporters to bigger daily papers and the Internet.
Barbara Stratford had worked at the Bay Guardian for a long time.
The narrator's mother asked Ron: "Will you come with us, Ron? Will you tell her Darryl's story?"
Ron shook off Dad's attempt to put a hand on his shoulders, saying he needed to clean himself up.
Ron came back downstairs shaved, with his hair gelled back, wearing a crisp military dress uniform with a row of campaign ribbons.
Ron smelled a little of beer, as if it were coming through his pores.
The group arrived at Barbara Stratford's driveway at midnight; she lived out of town in Mountain View.
The route to Mountain View was down the 101, past high-tech buildings.
The narrator contrasted this suburban landscape with the Bay Area they lived in, noting there were no homeless people pushing shopping carts and not even sidewalks.
